lead: she was not the only person you promised something to that afternoon. the boy was seven, named out loud, in front of the same room, and only one of them had a court that could end it.
sun: neither was a term of the other. you did not take the boy on as part of what marrying her involved, and she was never the route to him. both were entered at full weight in the same hour, by somebody with no instrument for putting one promise second. so when the marriage came apart at fourteen years, the other undertaking was not weakened by a degree, having never leaned on it.
moon: one of the two had paperwork behind it and could be ended by a judge in an afternoon. the other was an oath said out loud, which is the kind The Crown keeps, and nothing in you produces a way to stand down from one. the endable bond is on record as over, and the other goes on being kept by somebody who has no standing to keep it.
pull: the court ended the marriage and had nothing to say about the boy, because nobody had written the second promise down. he is thirty-one, and you have missed no year of him.
tension: there is no word for what you are to him now, and the two on offer are both wrong in the same direction. her family had you down for years as somebody who would not accept a decision, and the boy's own version, at nineteen, was that you stayed out of guilt. what nobody has been shown is the afternoon itself, where two things were promised separately and only one was ever the kind a court could hold.
cost: he came through his twenties without once testing whether an adult's presence was contingent on something else holding. the marriage was the other thing kept in that house at the same weight, and she said so in its last year. you have entered nothing since. the one still running has no end in it, and nothing in you goes looking for one.

lead: the sheet goes up in the corridor once a year and the picks run in order of joining date, yours at the top, and each name on it gets exactly one box.
sun: two ends of the plant have been yours since you were twenty-seven, run properly, neither a sideline the other paid for. the sheet has a single box against each name. the first pick in the building gets spent on whichever end cannot be got any other way, and the other is put back together out of swaps and owed favours afterwards, every year, by the one person the system was built to reward.
moon: nobody argues with a joining date. what it confers is first refusal, an instrument for taking one thing before anyone else can, and it has never been able to hold what you actually do. an exception would have to be granted by somebody senior to you, and the date settles that. so the arrangement gets rebuilt every year out of favours, by the name at the top of the board.
pull: first refusal is the reward at the top of the list, and it refuses one thing at a time. you have needed two since before most of the names below you were hired.
tension: a lad with three years in waits through the whole list for the line you took and did not stay on, and the following week he sees the first name on the board working somewhere else as well. that reads one way from the floor. nobody puts it to you, because the date on the wall settles arguments here, so it gets said in the canteen and reaches you third-hand, softened, from somebody being kind.
cost: both ends of the plant have run for nineteen years without a week where one of them went uncovered, and none of that arrangement is on paper anywhere. the favours are owed to you personally and the date is not transferable, so what the place has is a date rather than a system, and the date retires.

lead: your mother's account of why it ended and your father's account of why it ended were both true, and you went the whole way into each of them, and nothing anywhere told you when either was known well enough.
sun: most people settle this early and quietly, by deciding which parent to believe, and the deciding is what makes the rest survivable. you took both, whole, and kept taking both. each version got years of your attention on its own terms, neither ever demoted to the thing the other was covering for, and twenty-six years have not produced a ranking between them. both ran the whole time, side by side.
moon: an account of a marriage does not survive being verified. every date checked against a third memory, every letter found, every aunt asked twice — each of those took something out of the thing you wanted to keep, and nothing in The Root says either was known well enough. so both came apart in your hands, at different speeds, and neither was the one you were prepared to lose.
pull: two enquiries carried at once, neither of which had anything in it that could say stop. what they were dismantling was the only account of yourself you had.
tension: your sister settled it at nineteen by choosing him, and has had ordinary sundays with one parent ever since, which is the arrangement on offer and the one you could not take. what you get called is unable to let anything go, and both of them said it, near the end. each had been asked the same question in eleven forms and had come to understand the asking as an accusation, which in the second decade it partly was.
cost: the whole of it exists, both halves, checked: what he did, what she did, and the fifteen years neither of them could see the other doing. it is accurate to the week. it was assembled out of the people it is about, and by the time it was finished there was nobody left willing to sit and hear it, including the two it would have explained.

lead: two of the contingents in that column have you on their books, and they step off within a quarter of an hour of each other, so the road gets walked twice by you and once by everybody else in it.
sun: the one you were taken into at nine and the one you helped start at thirty-one are both fully yours: the subs, the meetings, the hall on wet evenings. both cost the same evenings, and one has never been an excuse for missing the other. the arrangement runs into one hour a year in which each of them exists properly, and the two hours are the same hour, on the same road.
moon: from the pavement it is a single body passing, and that is what the day is for. inside it, contingents are arriving at the assembly ground while others break up at the far end, and your going back through it registers on nobody watching. what registers is the count each of them takes of its own. you are on two of those and on the town's total once.
pull: both count you as theirs and the town counts you once. being in both means spending the day going the wrong way through people who are all going one way.
tension: the photograph on each of their walls is taken at the step-off, and you are in one of them a year, alternately, which the newer lot have noticed and the older lot have always known. the word used in both halls is stretched, said kindly, and the remedy offered has not varied in twenty years. neither hall has seen the sheet with both sets of timings on it that you have been walking off since you were thirty-one.
cost: the newer one came through the years when it was nine people because somebody in it also had weight in the older one, and both are still on that road. what you hold of the day is two halves, from different points of the route, and no year of it entire. everybody who walks it once comes home with one long afternoon. yours comes home in pieces.
